study_context_population.mission_platform: Generic CubeSat system used as an illustrative space mission architecture case.
study_context_population.size_form_factor: CubeSat; exact U-size/form factor not reported.

study_context_population.organization_type: Academic author affiliations are reported (Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology and MIT), but the case mission organization is not reported.

mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.stated_objective_pain_point: Demonstrate management of digital engineering information exchange for a CubeSat, represent subsystems/interfaces/objects/processes/states in DSM/DMM, and facilitate digital information flow from MBSE to PLM lifecycle stages.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.other_modeling_scope: Digital engineering information exchange and OPM-to-CPM ontology mapping across MBSE and PLM.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.system_boundary_abstraction: Whole CubeSat architecture is decomposed to major subsystems, then a Thermal Control System is decomposed into heater, radiator, controller/structure, and temperature sensor; the Radiator is represented as a CPM artifact at detailed design. EPS details, physical implementation, verification, operations, and actual mission design data are outside the reported boundary.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.required_prior_behavioral_domain_knowled: Not explicitly discussed as a requirement. The method encodes minimal behavior as OPM processes and states (for example heating/cooling and Tsat ranges) and carries object/process/state information across lifecycle models.
generality_reuse_mechanism: specific-mission model with reusable method only
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.generality_reuse_rationale: The same representation principles are applied at system and subsystem levels, and OPM information is mapped/transformed to DSM/DMM and CPM.

generality_reuse_mechanism_v1_1_reasonin.rationale: The paper supports a reusable method/workflow for OPM-to-DSM/DMM-to-CPM information exchange, using high-level and interface-focused representations. The worked model remains a CubeSat/Thermal Control/Radiator case, so it should be treated as a specific-mission/model case with a reusable method, not as a reusable mission-agnostic architecture or template. The paper does not directly justify low-dynamics/non-detailed behavior as a reuse mechanism.

evidence.quote: The utility of the proposed approach is that it keeps the same principles regardless of the level of decomposition.
from MBSE (a high-level abstraction of the system presented in Figure 3) to PLM (a detailed design, presented for one of the subsystems - Radiator shown in Figure 6).

claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.claim_text: DSM/DMM can represent CubeSat subsystems, interfaces, objects, processes, and states in one concise representation.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.artifact_process_linked: OPM object-process-state model transformed/encoded as DSM/DMM for the Thermal Control System interface/function/state representation.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.observed_effect_size_or_qualitative_effe: The matrix representation identifies mechanical/energy interfaces and associates heating/cooling processes with state changes for the thermal-control subsystem.

evidence_source.quote: A practical utility of Figure 5 is the ability to represent the CubeSat subsystems and their interfaces including objects/processes/states in one DSM/DMM representation.
The DSM part of the Figure 5 demonstrates that the controller/structure has the interfaces with every other subsystem (heater, radiator, and temperature sensor) mechanical (M), and energy (E).

claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.threats_or_alternative_explanations: The result demonstrates representability in a simplified subsystem example; it does not show scalability, correctness against an independent model, or measurable integration benefit.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.reliability_subtype_rationale: One coherent DSM/DMM representation is a model consistency/completeness claim, not EPS reliability.

claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.claim_text: The approach facilitates a digital information flow or digital thread from MBSE conceptual design to PLM/detailed design.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.artifact_process_linked: OPM/DSM/DMM conceptual model elements are mapped to CPM Radiator artifact behavior, function, form, geometry, material, and flow, and to an OPM-CPM DSM ontology map.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.observed_effect_size_or_qualitative_effe: The paper traces the cooling process and related state information from the conceptual model to CPM entities for the Radiator and then maps OPM and CPM ontologies in Figure 7.

evidence_source.quote: Based on the data that is encoded in DSM/DMM in Figure 5 we could trace the flow of data that was created during the conceptual design phase to the next phase of the design process.
Thus, Figure 7 demonstrates a mapping between all the entities of OPM and CPM ontologies.

claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.threats_or_alternative_explanations: The mapping is shown as a matrix/table, but no executable exchange, round-trip synchronization, or downstream engineering validation is reported.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.reliability_subtype_rationale: The claim is about traceability, lifecycle continuity, and interoperability.

claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.claim_text: The proposed DSM-based exchange approach may reduce complexity and errors associated with different ontologies in different design tools and expose exchange gaps.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.artifact_process_linked: DSM/DMM and OPM-CPM ontology map used to relate entities and detect gaps between conceptual and detailed-design ontologies.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.observed_effect_size_or_qualitative_effe: Qualitative claim only: complexity/error reduction is asserted as an expected utility; no measured reduction is reported.

evidence_source.quote: A proposed approach might serve as an effective method to reduce complexity associated with different ontologies in different design tools.

It allows to notice gaps in the data exchange between ontologies which are used at the appropriate stages of product development, and determine relationships that are necessary in order to most fully and representatively transfer data from the stage of conceptual design to the detailed design.

claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.threats_or_alternative_explanations: The matrix may make relationships visible, but the paper provides no baseline complexity measure, error data, or user evaluation.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.reliability_subtype_rationale: The claim is limited to generic ontology/data-exchange error or gap reduction; it is not EPS or mission reliability.

claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.claim_text: The approach can help engage digital tools in a concurrent engineering environment.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.artifact_process_linked: Complementary ontologies and DSM relationships proposed as a basis for a digital engineering environment.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.observed_effect_size_or_qualitative_effe: No observed effect; concurrent-engineering application is asserted in the abstract and deferred to future work.

evidence_source.quote: Ultimately, it allows engaging digital tools in a concurrent engineering environment.

In future work, we will apply the proposed approach to more complex systems being developed in a concurrent engineering design environment facilitating a specific space system design session from the very beginning of the design process to the detailed design stage. We will also be planning to apply the proposed approach to extended system lifecycle phases.

claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.reliability_subtype_rationale: The claim concerns concurrent-engineering tool engagement, not reliability.

claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.observed_effect_size_or_qualitative_effe: The method is shown at CubeSat system level and then at Thermal Control System level; reuse across independent missions is not demonstrated.

key_findings_by_rq.RQ1: Provides a system-level CubeSat architecture modeling and digital information exchange approach using OPM/OPCloud, DSM/DMM, and CPM. It is relevant to general CubeSat mission modeling and MBSE-to-PLM continuity, not to EPS-specific generic modeling.
key_findings_by_rq.RQ2: Claims integrability, traceability, lifecycle continuity, complexity/error reduction, and concurrent-engineering support, but evidence is illustrative and not EPS-specific; no reliability/reproducibility metrics are provided.
key_findings_by_rq.RQ3: No EPS verification procedures, pre-physical V&V artifacts, or integration/test readiness are modeled.

limitations_gaps_stated_by_authors: Future work will apply the method to more complex systems.
Future work will apply it in a concurrent engineering design environment and design session.
Future work will apply it to extended system lifecycle phases.
extractor_identified_limitations_gaps: Single illustrative CubeSat/Thermal Control System/Radiator case.
No EPS-specific modeling despite Power System being listed in the top-level decomposition.
No V&V artifacts or pre-physical verification mechanism.
No quantitative metrics, baseline comparator, independent validation, or physical/flight evidence.
Interoperability is semantic/conceptual rather than demonstrated executable tool exchange.

direct_evidence_quotes.quote: The specific objective of our paper is to demonstrate an approach of managing a digital engineering information exchange for a CubeSat system.
Another specific objective of our paper is to present the CubeSat subsystems and their interfaces including objects/processes/states in one DSM/DMM representation.

the goal of our work is to demonstrate how the proposed approach facilitates a digital information flow through different product lifecycle stages - from the Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) [8] to the product lifecycle management (PLM) [9] phases.
Based on the data that is encoded in DSM/DMM in Figure 5 we could trace the flow of data that was created during the conceptual design phase to the next phase of the design process.

It allows to notice gaps in the data exchange between ontologies which are used at the appropriate stages of product development, and determine relationships that are necessary in order to most fully and representatively transfer data from the stage of conceptual design to the detailed design.

In future work, we will apply the proposed approach to more complex systems being developed in a concurrent engineering design environment facilitating a specific space system design session from the very beginning of the design process to the detailed design stage. We will also be planning to apply the proposed approach to extended system lifecycle phases.
